To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Dense trajectory features are very useful for action recognition; (2) Fisher vector encoding is an efficient way to represent dense trajectory features; and (3) spatio-temporal pyramid is useful to embed structure information into Fisher vector representation.
the dense trajectory features, combined with Fisher vector and spatio-temporal pyramid, can achieve state of the art results in the THUMOS action recognition problem.
the combination of dense trajectory features and Fisher vector representations leads to state-of-the-art performance on the THUMOS 2013 dataset.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) how to efficiently extract dense trajectory features from video data; (2) how to integrate the local features into a compact representation with Fisher vector; (3) how to use the spatio-temporal structure information to improve the action representation; (4) how to use SVM for multi-class action classification.
